title: The coolest use for the Vision Pro
author: robbiet480
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: One day there will hopefully be a house on this land

Over the last year, I admittedly haven’t used my Vision Pro a ton, but fairly recently I discovered a super handy use that it’s absolutely incredible at, provided you have the right tools. After years of apartment life my girlfriend and I have recently begun the process of building our (first! exciting!) home, which is an absolute whirlwind of choices and decisions. Maybe it’s where we’re both programmers, but particularly for me, my software-oriented brain feels almost incompatible with this world of designing a home (she’s the main one keeping this project moving forward). In software if you don’t end up liking a feature after playing around with it for awhile, you can tweak it or remove it entirely (try doing that with a poorly placed wall). Here, decisions feel huge and hard to commit to. On top of this, the housing market is really expensive right now in many parts of the world (ours definitely included) so making good use of every square foot feels paramount. (Don’t worry, we have a great architect who guides us skillfully, but ultimately it’s up to us to sign off on everything!) Enter the Vision Pro Looking at PDFs of potential floor plans, you don’t (or at least I don’t) develop much of a sense of scale or connections with a bunch of black rectangles. This room says it’s 13 feet by 15 feet, I guess I can get out a measuring tape, but what does that feel like? Would this hallway be cramped? What all can you see when you first walk into the house? Then it hit me: virtual reality! There’s other VR devices that have better gaming chops, but I’m not sure there’s a consumer device out there that’s better than the Vision Pro on paper when it comes to rendering a virtual world with its high resolution screens and then placing you in it with its abundance of sensors. Problem is, how do you go from floor plan to virtual reality? Let’s get creatin’ I have a bit of experience using Fusion 360 (free 3D modeling software for hobbyists), so I had the idea to try to quickly build the floor plan up in 3D. Nothing fancy, just floors, ceilings, and walls, with holes for doors. If you’re not familiar with 3D design tools, this is a great first project, you’re basically just drawing the floor plan out in 2D and then extruding out the walls. YouTube and asking AI questions are awesome resources for learning this handy skill in 2026. Sites like Fiverr are also a great resource, I’m sure there’s an abundance of people there who could take a floor plan you’re interested in and turn it into a 3D file for a reasonable price.

Leveling it up A bunch of walls, ceilings, and holes in the wall is pretty powerful, but without actual objects or texture in the space it’s still a bit hard to get scale when you’re “walking around”. You know how you walk into an empty apartment for the first time and you’re like “Holy crap there’s so much room” and then you add your belongings and there suddenly isn’t? It’s kinda like that, we need to add some models and materials to the space to actually ground our perspective a bit and give things scale, otherwise it feels like walking around a warehouse. Adding textures Quick easy one. In Fusion, tap the “A” key to bring up the Appearance panel and you can drag and drop a bunch of common textures like wood, stone, or paint onto objects. This can really help to break up the monotony of everything being the same dull texture and actually gives the place depth. There’s even glass textures for windows which is pretty handy.

IKEA I can model a counter or a kitchen island (just a bunch of rectangles) but anything beyond that and I’m tapping out. Thankfully IKEA has a massive amount of furniture with corresponding 3D models, and even if you’re not a big IKEA person (wow aren’t you fancy) having any approximation for your final furniture in your place really helps you get an idea of how things fit together and can be positioned.
summaryZh: One day there will hopefully be a house on this land

comments.author: jondiggsit
comments.textRawHtml:
My team uses this technology on a daily basis at my company. I run a design / build firm in the Hamptons, USA. We start all of our design projects with a 3d-first approach. Schematic design starts in 3D using Rhino3D or Revit. We use visualization plugins, like Enscape, to render the models and stream to a Quest 3 headset.

So when clients come in, and feels adventurous, we'll setup the headset, set the display height to their actual, and let them walk around their beautiful new home.

The response has been powerful. My clients are able to truly understand the scale, the proportion of rooms, ceiling heights, and the smallest details.

We're able to make real-time changes to the model (within reason) and provide instant design feedback.

I've been using this technology for years and I'm surprised it's not being adopted faster - good for us right now though!
comments.textZhHtml:
我的团队每天在我的公司使用这项技术。我在美国汉普顿经营一家设计/建造公司。我们以 3D 优先的方法开始所有设计项目。使用 Rhino3D 或 Revit 以 3D 形式开始原理图设计。我们使用 Enscape 等可视化插件来渲染模型并传输到 Quest 3 耳机。

因此，当客户进来并感到有冒险精神时，我们将设置耳机，将显示高度设置为他们的实际高度，然后让他们在美丽的新家周围走动。

反应非常强烈。我的客户能够真正了解规模、房间比例、天花板高度和最小的细节。

我们能够对模型进行实时更改（在合理范围内）并提供即时设计反馈。

我已经使用这项技术多年，但我很惊讶它没有被更快地采用 - 不过现在对我们来说有好处！

children.author: wlesieutre
children.textRawHtml:
Revit is parametric, but something like Rhino (going off reputation, never used it myself) gives you more free-form modeling control.

It’s like starting with a pencil sketch instead of going straight to SolidWorks, once you start building that more nailed down drawing with its explicit flow of sketches and operations in relationship to each other, it becomes much harder to make large structural changes.

https://help.autodesk.com/view/RVT/2023/ENU/?guid=GUID-71F2C...
children.textZhHtml:
Revit是参数化的，但像Rhino这样的软件（仅凭口碑，我自己没用过）能让你更自由地控制建模。

这就像先用铅笔打草稿，而不是直接上手SolidWorks，一旦你开始绘制那种更确定的图纸，其草图和操作流程之间有着明确的关联，再进行大规模的结构改动就会困难得多。

https://help.autodesk.com/view/RVT/2023/ENU/?guid=GUID-71F2C...

children.author: adfm
children.textRawHtml: Rhino + Grasshopper is the gold standard for all the curvy geometry in anything resembling Zaha Hadid’s work. It is also parametric. There’s even a plug-in to use it inside Revit. Solidworks is great for designing the chassis, but the body was probably sketched in Rhino or Maya.
children.textZhHtml: Rhino + Grasshopper是打造所有类似扎哈·哈迪德作品中那些曲面几何体的黄金标准。它也是参数化的。甚至还有一个插件可以在Revit内部使用它。Solidworks非常适合设计底盘，但车身外观可能是在Rhino或Maya中勾勒出来的。

children.author: embedding-shape
children.textRawHtml:
> pursue my original passion in architecture

Do it! You have the knowledge, you have the interest, you now have confirmation someone else was able to do it, so can you! No time to wait, just jump in and start planning, then execute! I don't know why people hesitate so much, you do literally only live once, and who has time to sit around thinking "what if?" when we're old and just want to chill? Worst case scenario, you fail, learned a bunch, lean back on what supported you before, maybe in a slightly different way, but with so many more fun memories.
children.textZhHtml:
>追求我对建筑最初的热情

去做吧！你有知识，你有兴趣，你现在已经确认其他人能够做到这一点，你也可以！没有时间等待，只需开始计划，然后执行！我不知道为什么人们如此犹豫，人实际上只活一次，谁有时间坐下来思考“如果呢？”当我们老了只想放松一下？最坏的情况是，你失败了，学到了很多东西，依靠以前支持你的东西，也许以稍微不同的方式，但有更多有趣的回忆。

children.author: jve
children.textRawHtml:
Uhh, I have a laptop near me where I was planning to throw my drawing to get a 3D model in blender. I have no experience with blender, but I have a dwg file architect gave me (for a house where I already live in) and I was ready to make AI do the rest. I want to make some reconstruction, plan to buy/calculate stuff I need for the walls/floor, etc and just a fun project to visualize my home.

Anyways, I learned that AI can't read DWG, so converted it to DXF using trial AutoCAD. The LibreCAD couldn't even open my dwg as it was some newer version.

I also have a plan to make some "what-if" scenarios - we want to remodel kitchen, remove this wall, put this here and there... basically that can help visualize and that can understand how big stuff is to calculate BOM and such.

Is Blender OK for it or should I target some SketchUp for my "3D feel"? I'm looking forward to using some free tools.

Is there even a free cad alternative that would understand "newer" dwg file formats? Is there other software than AutoCAD with MCP capability that would allow navigate dwg/dxf?
children.textZhHtml:
呃，我手边正好有台笔记本电脑，本来打算把图纸扔进去，用Blender建个3D模型。我完全没用过Blender，不过建筑师给了我一份dwg格式的文件（就是我现在住的这套房子的），我本来打算让AI把剩下的活儿都包了。我想搞点改造，计划算算、买买墙面和地板需要的材料之类的，顺便就当是个好玩的项目，把我的家做个3D可视化。

总之，我发现AI无法读取DWG文件，于是用AutoCAD试用版将其转换成了DXF格式。另外，LibreCAD甚至都打不开我的dwg文件，因为那是个较新的版本。

我还有个计划，打算做一些“假设”场景——比如我们想改造厨房，拆掉这面墙，把东西挪到这儿挪到那儿……基本上这能帮我们直观地看到效果，弄清楚各种东西的实际尺寸，以便计算物料清单之类的。

Blender做这个合适吗，还是说为了追求那种“3D感”，我应该改用SketchUp？我很期待能用上一些免费工具。

到底有没有免费的CAD替代软件能兼容“较新”的dwg文件格式？除了AutoCAD之外，还有没有其他具备MCP功能、可以浏览dwg/dxf文件的软件？

children.author: jondiggsit
children.textRawHtml:
You are 100% correct. My company is fortunate enough to have the working capital and time to explore ideas, which is honestly, one of the most fulfilling parts of my business.

And the Hamptons competition is very serious. It's insane really. Construction in the Hamptons is the Olympics of high-end building. There are atleast a dozen excellent, amazing builders and over 250 active companies in total. My company sits near the top of that list and the only one, to my knowledge, actively leveraging technology to our advantage.

No private heli-pads, they banned it long ago. There's a little known heli-pad on Meadow Lane in Southampton. So from your SoHo office to your beachfront house is under an hour. There's also Blade service to EH.

One of my clients often arrives by seaplane to check on the progress of his Peconic Bay waterfront project. It's pretty cool.
children.textZhHtml:
您说得完全正确。我们公司非常幸运，拥有充足的营运资金和时间去探索各种新想法，说实话，这也是我事业中最具成就感的环节之一。

汉普顿地区的竞争异常激烈，简直到了疯狂的地步。这里的建筑工程堪称高端建筑界的“奥运会”。当地至少有十几家出类拔萃、实力雄厚的承建商，活跃的公司总数更是超过250家。我的公司在这份名单中名列前茅，而且据我所知，我们是唯一一家积极借助科技手段打造竞争优势的企业。

没有私人直升机停机坪，早就被禁了。南安普顿的梅多巷有个鲜为人知的直升机停机坪。所以从你苏荷区的办公室到海滨别墅，全程不到一小时。此外，还有飞往EH的Blade直升机服务。

我的一位客户经常乘水上飞机过来，查看他在佩科尼克湾滨水项目的进展。这挺酷的。
